blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Coriolis force is an apparent force caused by Earth's rotation from west to east.
It deflects freely moving objects to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere.
The magnitude of the Coriolis force increases with latitude, reaching zero at the equator and maximum at the poles.
The force acts perpendicular to the direction of motion and affects wind direction, not wind speed.
Absence of Coriolis force at the equator prevents the formation of tropical cyclones in the 0°–5° latitude belt.

blocks.content: The Coriolis force deflects fluids to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere due to Earth's rotation.

items: Why do tropical cyclones not originate at the equator? Because the Coriolis force is zero at 0° latitude, preventing cyclonic vortex formation.
Ferrel's Law states that any fluid moving horizontally in the Northern Hemisphere is deflected to its right, and in the Southern Hemisphere to its left.
Coriolis force is directly proportional to wind velocity and the sine of latitude (F ∝ v sin φ).
